reason: S1 adds the public DNS URI-record parser ares_parse_uri_reply, but H0 invokes only the pre-existing ares_parse_*_reply functions and never calls this new entry point. Consequently, fuzz input cannot reach or control the newly introduced URI parsing path, including record-length handling, allocation, string copying, linked-list construction, and error cleanup. This gap did not exist in S0 because ares_parse_uri_reply was introduced by the commit.
evidence: include/ares.h newly declares ares_parse_uri_reply(const unsigned char *abuf, int alen, struct ares_uri_reply **uri_out).
src/lib/ares_parse_uri_reply.c is a new 184-line parser consuming attacker-controlled DNS bytes, including rr_len, DNS__16BIT fields, ares_malloc(rr_len-3), strncpy, and linked-list cleanup.

H0 calls ares_parse_a_reply, ares_parse_aaaa_reply, ares_parse_ptr_reply, ares_parse_ns_reply, ares_parse_srv_reply, ares_parse_mx_reply, ares_parse_txt_reply, ares_parse_soa_reply, ares_parse_naptr_reply, and ares_parse_caa_reply, but not ares_parse_uri_reply.
ARES_DATATYPE_URI_REPLY and its allocation/free handling are newly added to ares_data.h and ares_data.c specifically to support the uncovered parser.
recommended_action: Extend H0 to call ares_parse_uri_reply(data, size, &uri) and release any non-NULL result with ares_free_data(uri).
